facts.agency: City of Port Alder Department of Permitting & Inspections
facts.title: AI-Assisted Permit Intake and Review Automation Platform
facts.summary: The City of Port Alder is seeking a qualified firm to design, build, deploy, and support a cloud-hosted, AI-assisted platform for permit intake and plan review. The goal is to streamline the permit application process, reducing incomplete submissions and cutting down the median time from submission to first review. The platform will automate completeness checks, assist plan reviewers by extracting data and flagging potential code conflicts, and provide applicant support without replacing licensed human reviewers.
facts.scope_of_work: The Contractor will deliver a cloud-hosted platform that: (a) guides applicants through submitting complete permit packages; (b) uses AI to perform completeness checks within 2 minutes and extract key data; (c) routes packages to review queues; and (d) assists City plan reviewers by flagging code conflicts with citations. The project includes an applicant portal, a conversational assistant (English and Spanish mandatory; Vietnamese and Russian desired), a staff dashboard, notifications, two-way integration with PermitCore v9, GIS lookup, state contractor license checking, data migration of ~3,200 open applications (1.4 TB), export for Power BI reporting, user training, and post-launch support/stabilization. Work is divided into Phase 1 (Discovery), Phase 2 (Pilot release for 10 permit types), Phase 3 (Full release), and Phase 4 (Stabilization). Field inspection mobile apps, replacement of PermitCore, permit fee payment processing, and hardware procurement are out of scope.
facts.contract_value: Not-to-exceed amount of $420,000 for implementation (Phases 1–4) plus the first two years of subscription, hosting and support.
facts.period_of_performance: Three (3) years from Notice to Proceed, with two optional one-year renewals at the City's discretion.
facts.place_of_performance: The Project Manager must attend the project kickoff in person in Port Alder. All other work may be performed remotely from within the United States. All City data must be stored and processed in data centers located in the United States.
facts.how_to_submit: Submit through Port Alder Bids. The proposal must consist of one text-searchable PDF of no more than 30 pages (excluding attachments and cost proposal) containing Tabs 1–8. Submit the cost proposal (Attachment C) as a separate file. Emailed, faxed, or paper proposals will not be accepted. Specific page limits within the PDF: Tab 1 (2 pages), Tab 2 (4 pages), Tab 3 (12 pages), Tab 4 (5 pages), Tab 5 (3 pages, excluding resumes), Tab 6 (2 pages), Tab 7 (2 pages), Tab 8 (no limit stated). Do not include pricing anywhere else in the proposal except Attachment C.

score_factors.reason: The scope focuses on AI automation platforms, web/mobile intake portals, and compliance tooling, matching our primary build capabilities.
All work except the project kickoff can be performed remotely from within the United States.
$420,000 budget for implementation and initial support is appropriate for a small senior team.
Must confirm mandatory qualifications such as 3 years in business, 3 past references, and SOC 2 Type II hosting environment.

what_would_change_decision: We do not meet the minimum requirement of 3 years in business.
We lack the required 3 references, including at least two past projects delivering AI/workflow software for public-sector or regulated clients.
We cannot provide a hosting environment with a valid SOC 2 Type II or FedRAMP authorization.
We cannot meet the mandatory insurance coverage requirements ($1M/$2M CGL, $2M E&O, $2M Cyber).
We do not qualify under the Small Business self-certification threshold (<100 employees and <$15M gross receipts).
Our Project Manager cannot attend the kickoff meeting in person in Port Alder.
open_questions: Will sample security documentation submitted under Tab 8 count toward the overall 30-page PDF limit specified in Section 5.2?
How should proposers code compliance in Attachment D for requirement FR-7, which lists email notifications as mandatory and SMS notifications as desired within a single row?

ambiguities.issue: The table of contents on Page 2 lists Section 7 as 'Budget, Contract Term and Payment' and Section 8 as 'Insurance', but the main text section heading on Page 11 lists '7. BUDGET, CONTRACT TERM AND PAYMENT' and on Page 12 lists '8. INSURANCE' while using numbering '9. GENERAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS' for Section 9, creating slight structural mapping ambiguity, though titles match.

Section 3.2 lists requirement FR-7 Notifications as type 'M / D' (Email mandatory, SMS desired), but in Attachment D (Requirements Response Matrix) on Page 16, it is listed as 'M / D' without separate rows, leaving it ambiguous how to code compliance for the mandatory versus desired portion.

Section 5.2 specifies a 30-page limit for the PDF excluding attachments and cost proposal, and lists page limits per tab totaling 30 pages (Tabs 1-7). However, Tab 8 includes 'Attachments A, B, D and E, and sample security documentation' without specifying whether sample security documentation counts toward the 30-page limit or is considered an excluded attachment.
